chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Maghra, from Abu Basir who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the bequest for the inheritor, so he said: It is permissible.

key_terms.الْوَارِثِ: The inheritor (warith) — a legal heir entitled to a fixed share under the laws of inheritance
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةِ: Bequest or testament (wasiyya) — a testamentary disposition of property to take effect after death
key_terms.تَجُوزُ: It is permissible (tajuz) — jurisprudential term indicating that an act is legally allowed

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to make a bequest in favor of an inheritor in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Abu Basir asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) whether making a bequest (wasiyya) in favor of one's legal inheritor is permissible. The Imam concisely affirmed that such a bequest is lawful, addressing a question that arose because some jurists debated whether a bequest could supplement the fixed inheritance shares. This ruling clarifies that a testator may direct additional gifts to heirs beyond their Quranic shares.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al Magra, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the bequest for the inheritor. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: (it is) ‘Permissible’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu al-Mighra’ from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if one can make a will for the heir.
